clue.text: Quiet and subdued outside farm building

indicators.note: outside tells us the word for subdued wraps around the word for quiet

parts.note: cowed means intimidated into submission, subdued
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A hushed, cowed figure stands outside a barn on a farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelter where cattle are housed is a typical outbuilding on a farm.

clue.text: Officer I located in Scottish island

indicators.note: located in tells us the word for I goes inside the island's name

parts.note: Coll is an island of the Inner Hebrides in Scotland
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An officer is stationed on a remote Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: An army officer ranking above a lieutenant colonel and below a brigadier.

clue.text: Pardon me, do you stock anything similar?

parts.note: what? is an informal way of saying pardon me when you mishear
a shopper asking whether a shop stocks something says have you

explanation.surface: A customer asks a shopkeeper whether they have anything like it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is tacked on to a list to mean and other similar things, much like and so on.

clue.text: Body snatcher gets address for woman in quarters reserved for females

parts.note: William Hare, with Burke, was a notorious Edinburgh body snatcher
Ms is a form of address for a woman

explanation.surface: A grave robber chases a woman into the women's quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: Burke and Hare were 1820s Edinburgh murderers who sold corpses to anatomists.
explanation.definitionFit: The secluded women's section of a Muslim household is called by this word.

clue.text: Wanted hole repaired, as looking scruffy

indicators.note: repaired means put back together, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone wanted a hole in their clothes mended, as they looked a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from shoes worn at the heels, means shabby and neglected in appearance.

clue.text: Second record needed work not yet completed

parts.note: to second a proposal is to back or support it
a log is a written record, as in a ship's log

explanation.surface: An office needs a second record to track its unfinished jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like a noun or an ordinal, but here it is the verb meaning to support.
explanation.definitionFit: An accumulation of tasks still waiting to be done is exactly what this word names.

clue.text: Tolerate pub being invaded by English

indicators.note: the pub is invaded, so the letter for English goes inside it

parts.note: a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: Locals must put up with their pub being overrun by English visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to endure or put up with it.

clue.text: Turning up, we borrow a hundred pounds for a few personal lines

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reverses the whole string so it reads upward

parts.note: taken as written
to hire is to borrow for payment
written as a sum, a hundred pounds is the pound sign L (from Latin libra) followed by C, the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Someone turns up having borrowed a hundred pounds to write a short note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning up' reverses WEHIRELC into the answer, read upward in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A clerihew is a comic four-line verse about a named person, so a few lines on a personality.

clue.text: Flower arrangements produce cash for Romanians

definitions.meaning: Hawaiian garlands of flowers worn round the neck
the plural of leu, the Romanian currency unit

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both Hawaiian flower garlands and units of Romanian money.

clue.text: Ship of the line girl joined a long time later

parts.note: gal is an informal word for girl
an eon is an immensely long time

explanation.surface: A girl joins a ship of the line and stays for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ship of the line' reads as a naval phrase, but only 'Ship' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A large sailing ship with several decks, used especially by Spain from the 15th to 18th centuries.

clue.text: Area of Tyrolean meadow

indicators.note: an area of the word Tyrolean is a stretch of its letters, so the answer sits inside it

explanation.surface: A patch of Alpine pasture in the Tyrol.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic and crossword word for a grassy field or pasture.

clue.text: Alarm waiter, changing order for something uncooked

indicators.note: changing the order of the letters signals that they are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A restaurant customer alarms the waiter by ordering something raw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing order' plays on a diner changing their order, but it tells you to rearrange ALARM WAITER.
explanation.definitionFit: Unprocessed material is literally uncooked stuff, so the phrase is a playful fit for anything not yet cooked.

clue.text: He-man — he and I concocted a book

indicators.note: concocted means made up or mixed together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A muscleman and two others cook up a story together.
explanation.definitionFit: Nehemiah is a book of the Old Testament, named after the Jewish governor who rebuilt Jerusalem's walls.

clue.text: Instrument for doctor

definitions.meaning: a violin is a stringed instrument, informally called by this name
to doctor accounts is to falsify or tamper with them

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a violin and, as a verb, to cook or falsify figures, as doctor does.

clue.text: "Go downhill and stop' — I speak formally

parts.note: to deter is to stop or discourage
taken as written
to orate is to make a formal speech

explanation.surface: A speaker formally urges people to stop going downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: To worsen or decline is figuratively to go downhill.

clue.text: Curmudgeon lays burden down on bed

indicators.note: in a down clue, down on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: a cross to bear is a burden
a patch is a garden bed, as in a vegetable patch

explanation.surface: A grumpy old man lays down his load on his bed.
explanation.definitionFit: An irritable, bad-tempered person is a crosspatch, much like a curmudgeon.

clue.text: Charged, but not recorded

definitions.meaning: an electrically charged wire is described as a ... one
a broadcast that is not recorded goes out as it happens

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both carrying electric current and broadcast in real time rather than prerecorded.

clue.text: Dance in case ferryman comes round

indicators.note: the ferryman's name comes round, enclosing, the phrase for in case

parts.note: Charon is the ferryman of the dead across the Styx in Greek myth
lest means in case, for fear that

explanation.surface: A boatman goes round a case while dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in case' looks like a container signal but is the fodder: LEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively 1920s dance named after the city in South Carolina.

clue.text: Left for dead

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both having gone away and, euphemistically, deceased.

clue.text: Relocated in Leeds area, head of Yorkshire educational system

indicators.note: relocated means moved to a new place, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone moves to the Leeds area, at the head of a Yorkshire school system.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds is a city in Yorkshire, which makes the surface geographic; the letters of LEEDS AREA plus Y are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A British scheme letting employees take time off work for study at college is known by this phrase.

clue.text: Change direction and cross over entrance

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the string is turned upside down

parts.note: to yaw is to swing off course, changing direction
a rood is a cross or crucifix

explanation.surface: Someone changes direction and crosses over to the entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses YAWROOD to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening in a wall by which one enters a room or building.

clue.text: King has dismissed one carriage

indicators.note: dismissing a letter means removing it from the king's name

parts.note: Priam was king of Troy in Greek legend
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A monarch sends away one of his coaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carriage' suggests a royal coach, but it means a baby carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A pram is a baby carriage, short for perambulator.

clue.text: Tangle, one closing administrative centre

parts.note: a mat is a tangled mass, as of hair
a lock is something that closes a door

explanation.surface: A knot of something closes off the town hall.
explanation.walkthrough: Matlock is the county town of Derbyshire, where the county council sits.
explanation.definitionFit: Matlock is Derbyshire's county town, its seat of local government.

clue.text: Wet a politician in retreat

indicators.note: in tells us a and the politician go inside the retreat

parts.note: a den is a private retreat
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A soft, wet politician is in retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wet' in British politics means a weak moderate, so it seems to describe the politician; here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To moisten something is to make it damp.

clue.text: Judge left off joking about eyes

indicators.note: left off means the letter for judge is dropped from the word for joking

parts.note: jocular means joking, humorous

explanation.surface: A judge stops joking and looks someone in the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to the eyes or vision, so concerning the eyes.

clue.text: Express oneself forcibly whether or not holding each king

annotationWithheld.clue: Express oneself forcibly whether or not holding each king

clue.text: Metal star

definitions.meaning: a heavy grey metal, chemical symbol Pb
the principal performer in a play or film

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a heavy metal and the leading role or star of a production.

clue.text: Be quiet for fear of work becoming very fast, with only brief pauses

definitions.text: very fast, with only brief pauses

parts.note: whist is an old exclamation meaning hush, be quiet
lest means for fear that
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A worker keeps quiet in case the job becomes a rush with hardly any breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: WHIST as a command to be silent is archaic; most know it only as the card game.
explanation.definitionFit: A tour making many quick stops, as a campaign train stopping briefly at small stations, is described this way.

clue.text: Being feeble, can't cut any dessert

definitions.meaning: the idiom for being ineffective is that one cuts no frozen water
a frozen sweet, as in an ... lolly or water ...

explanation.walkthrough: The first part is a fill-in-the-blank: someone feeble 'can't cut any' of the answer, the idiom for making no impression.
explanation.definitionFit: The word completes the idiom for having no effect, and also names a frozen dessert.

clue.text: Bother to take notice round

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone can't be bothered to take notice of what is going round.
explanation.definitionFit: Fuss or trouble, as in much ado about nothing, is a synonym for bother.

clue.text: Supplied eddy, 7 eddies

indicators.note: eddies as a verb means swirls round, so the letters are churned up

parts.note: the answer to 7 down is a word meaning Romanian money

explanation.surface: Water supplied an eddy, and then several more eddies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eddies' looks like a plural noun but is the anagram signal; LEI, the answer to 7 down, is shuffled with EDDY.
explanation.definitionFit: To have yielded a crop is to have produced or supplied it.

clue.text: Nag, horse at extremes of exhaustion, has to stumble

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: of a horse, to peck is to stumble on landing

explanation.surface: A horse, at the end of its tether, keeps stumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nag' and 'horse' suggest a single animal, but Nag is a verb, the definition, and horse means heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: To nag someone constantly is to henpeck them, as a domineering partner is said to do.
